texts.text: ... Wait, do you hear that? Sounds like a pair of scissors.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: It might be worth checking out.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <... Hey, Meursault. Do you still have that pair of scissors we got from the Alteration Shop last time?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes. However, its edges have chipped slightly in the process of cutting through the last Two-piece. We will require a new pair of scissors for that task.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <They were pretty tough, I guess...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <We need to cut through Two-piece if we want to proceed, so... looks like we'll be getting ourselves a new pair of scissors.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: This isn't where the noise is coming from, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: This isn't the way to the vendor, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Not this way, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Desire. Then it shall be donned.</color>
According to Miss Jeanne, it seems like each faction has a... guiding "Voice," who is, in truth, a "Giant." This voice probably belongs to one of them, too.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: A classic manipulation tactic. It bolsters solidarity within a faction by instilling its population with the entrenched in-group-versus-out-group mentality.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: It doesn't twinkle or dance anymore.
The corpse of a Rouge. Their veins have stopped writhing, turning dry and grey.
A slough of flesh is splayed on the ground. Looks like a popped balloon.
One has become two. The one who has become two stirs no longer.
Another shop, another boring, insipid dress made from flesh.

[Differential of Falling Series 2: "Siegel"
This installation was inspired by a Mannequin's fall through the Grand Magasin. The imagery evokes the falling continuity of time.]
Looking at it probably won't advance my understanding of it. ... Not that there's any need to.

[Differential of Falling Series 3: "Stockmann"
This installation was inspired by a Mannequin's fall through the Grand Magasin. The imagery evokes the falling continuity of time.
Sculpted in a smaller size relative to the Series 1 installation.]
A necklace that appears to be made of metal is on display.
A cash register. There doesn't seem to be anything left inside.
An unadorned mannequin torso.
A T-shirt dyed in a unique pattern. Haven't encountered a single Rouge who's wearing this.

[Le Président 67' Signature Collection.
An encapsulation of Le Rouge's unique choice of material and bygone heritages, this exceptional blending has established a unique yet fitting identity for itself in the age of change. - Please enquire a customer representative for more information on its price.]
It's a cash register. Reaching into its drawer to see if there's anything left... yields some eyeballs that were rolling around in its corner.
Not a bad get, Executive Manager. Take it—it should do us good to find and keep as many of these as we can.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Hm... Sure.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: W-wait, isn't this just straight-up thievery?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: A more accurate designation for this strategy would be "field requisition tactics."
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>I don't know, this strategy probably falls under the designation we call "larceny" here.</color>
... *cough*
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Wait, we're not allowed to take eyeballs from cash registers? What about all those Mannequins we kill—I mean, "helped to the exit"?>
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu, you mean "criminal damage to property"?</color>
<It doesn't matter inside this department store anyway, Sinclair. Take those eyeballs, Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Hah. You're no fun at all.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Just decided to ignore me now 'cuz you can't understand how jokes work, huh?</color>
Took the eyeballs.
Don't need these that badly.
There isn't anything left.
There's a caption below that says the following: [Treated and coated with fresh-melted fat tissue from a living subject. Touch it and feel the glassy, enamelistic surface.]
Obtained some eyeballs that fell through the cracks in the couch.
The price tag says "Sarcopenic Weight"
The label calls it [Seasonal Apparel]. Not that "seasons" mean anything.
Still looks like a lump of dough.
[68' Signature Collection. An unequivocal rejection of the revivalist philosophy that underlined the 67' Collection, and a consummation of the deconstructive quality that is quintessentially Rouge.]
Doesn't look so plush now.

[Differential of Falling Series 1: "Cynthia"
This installation depicts the fall of Cynthia, the first Mannequin to fall in the Grand Magasin. The only large-scale installation in the series, it sets itself apart from the rest of the series by being the only piece to depict the precise moment her fall began in painstaking detail.]
<Huh, now that I'm looking at it... this place has "installations," that aren't necessarily products.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Do you think the Ring... has any presence here?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Not all artistic endeavors are associated with the Ring's activities.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Still, these remind me of the things we saw back at the Ring Nursefather's gallery.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <Maybe there's a note explaining what all this means. Assuming that the note survived...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: There indeed seem to be other "Differential of Falling" series in this area...
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Well, they went out of their way to call it "Series 1," so it seems reasonable to assume that there's a "Series 2." Let's keep an eye out for it in case they have anything that might come in handy.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The label says [Off-Season Items].
Articles of clothing adorned with what appear to be bones.

["Les Oiseaux" Experimental Collection.]
The caption below reads that it was inspired by a bird. It is plastered from top to bottom with a thick coating of feathers—where did they even get the feathers?
There's a heavy curtain draped over this door. Can't seem to enter.
A gargantuan arm separated from somebody. Or something.
A brimmed hat that one might dare call "average."
A sundry of colorful threads line this wall.
The edge is very sharp. Almost like a scythe's edge rather than a scissor blade's.
A rusty pair of scissors. These haven't been used in a while.
The other side is hidden behind a thick layer of fabric. There's something twinkling there.
The other side is hidden behind a thick layer of fabric. Uncovered the fabric, but this time, there isn't anything behind.
The other side is hidden behind a thick layer of fabric.
There are numerous holes here. Possibly for plugging something in.
These haven't been connected in a while. The sockets are full of dust.
Each hole has a tag taped on top of it. There used to be something written on the tags, but now they're faded and illegible.
Don't hear anything.
Sounds like the hubbub of a distant crowd.
It's quiet. Must've mistaken some other sound.

This device looks like a ventilation fan. 
It's so dusty inside... Must have been out of order for a while.
There's a dusting of... dust inside the long gap.
Fallen debris is blocking the way. There's no way over or around it.
Don't know any games that use these dice.
Random pips and letters are scattered on its sides without rhyme or reason.
A useless, heavy die.
A weird die.
Huh, wonder what this is? Some kind of broadcast device?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <It's a communication switchboard.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What's a communication switchboard?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: ... Have you had access to one of these devices in the past, Executive Manager?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Uh... No, I just read about it in a pamphlet once.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... As expected of our Executive Manager! Your rising passion for learning is most admirable indeed.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Outis seems to consider something for a moment.
The way these tubes are lining the wall reminds me of a massive pipe organ.
Though I don't know if it's for listening or relaying but...
... imagining that someone might be listening in on my every word, giving me commands from where I can't see... a strange trepidation gurgles from the pit of my stomach.
The gaze is not beholden to the limitations of the sight, it seems.
Several birds lie beneath a long, trumpet-shaped tube.
<color=#cf0000>No... don't understand it... you mustn't understand...</color>
When I pick up one of the birds, the voice cuts off.
Obtained Dead Bird.
Something glints between the shafts of sunlight.
Meursault pulled out the glinting object. It's an old recorder.
... Is it just me, or is this coat shrinking?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Those are socks that have become quite popular among the customers on the fourth floor. The kind you can put on simply by wearing them.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: S-Socks? This is a coat!
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Functional socks. One merely slips them on without having to go through the trouble of bending over.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Hm, fascinating. Why don't we bring this along, Executive Manager? It doesn't belong to anyone anymore.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Sure.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It says [Origami CollectioN° 92, 3 of 5. Someone's fall sublimated into superpositioned time.]
[Origami CollectioN ° 92, 4 of 5.]
[Origami CollectioN ° 92, 2 of 5.]
<I think we saw the "1 of 5" of the series on the first floor.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh, right...! I remember learning about how some prints and sculptures are made with creating multiple identical copies in mind, only giving a different number to each "iteration" to distinguish them.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: And even though each piece is pretty much indistinguishable from one another, their value might vary depending on the number they're given.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Then... the one on the first floor must be the first copy.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Most unremarkable rabble would've walked past it without a second thought... What impeccable perception you have! I expected no less of our Executive Manager!
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text:
It says [Off-Season / Prêt-à-porter].
Still on sale.

It says [Off-Season / Prêt-à-porter].
Still on sale.
Huh, these clothes are more expensive than the others.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: That is because the display you are looking at is for this season's Prêt-à-porter items.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Prêt-à-por...ter?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Prêt-à-porter. It refers to made-to-stock, ready-to-wear items; those of higher quality and prestige, in particular.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <These don't look so expensive anymore...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: This couch is disturbingly shiny. No need to try slumping down on it.
... Don't feel like dredging through the gaps anymore. Decided to move on past it.
<color=#ebcaa2>... Still a busy bee, huh?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Pff... Do you really have to try so hard for loose change? Aren't you rich enough to ignore a handful of eyeballs?</color>
<... I can always afford to be richer, can't I?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The manager replies that they can always afford to be richer.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Took some eyeballs lodged deep inside.
Huh, look at the tags. These clothes are cheaper than the others.
Cloth straps wrapped around the figure make a faint straining noise.
... Did it just smile? Probably just seeing things...

This might look like a straitjacket, but it's not.
It's a formal suit.
Can they even see out of this thing?
Wait, the expression changed... A nameless terror crawls up my spine.
Just looks stuffy now.

This outfit is called [La Première Superposition].
Must be pretty popular among the Noirs.
Something's breathing from behind the fabric. Uncomfortable.
The Noirs at the checkout counter are wearing something similar to this outfit.

[La Troisieme Superposition. 
A fascinating blend of cape, frock coat, and jacket in a all-in-one integration. Highest prestige in this Season's collection.
Please visit the reception desk for pricing and reservations.]
Maybe we can afford it now...?

[La Troisieme Superposition. 
A fascinating blend of cape, frock coat, and jacket in a all-in-one integration. Highest prestige in this Season's collection.
Please visit the reception desk for pricing and reservations.]
[Prêt-à-porter. Contains 150% of the Golden Yarn compared to the Last Season's!]
Upon closer inspection, I notice that it contains only 0.00015% of the so-called "Golden Yarn." Doesn't seem anywhere near significant enough to warrant putting that on the advertisement.
Doesn't this mean that the last season's products had only 0.0001% Golden Yarn...?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: ... I'm willing to bet that Whale chips from U Corp. have more Whale in them than this has Golden Yarn.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: A display case full of glasses. Not sure how I'd go about wearing them, however.
... These are glasses, right...? The label above the display does say "glasses"...
On display are pairs of glasses and sunglasses. Some of these'll look good on Gregor.
Bizarrely normal-looking pairs of glasses and sunglasses that look out of place here. Surprisingly mundane, almost.
A combination of a stool and a drawer... A strawer. Looks like it fails at being either, though.
A combination of a stool and a drawer... A strawer. Found a handful of eyeballs in its drawer that somebody forgot.
A combination of a stool and a drawer... A strawer. Found a handful of eyeballs in its drawer that somebody forgot... not. A clock can hope, though.
It's done. You may take this Golden Fabric and its brilliance with you.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Easily ripped the spine off the Rouge who'd stopped moving.
Ah... I see your will and abide by it wholeheartedly. Today, once again, I will be honest with myself... and indulge in my desires.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: I shall stand against all that seeks to stop us, that one day your Voice might reach me, too...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: ... Do I hear new customers? First thing I like to tell the first-timers on our floor is this: you'll find the apparel displayed here to have a much more generous proportion of the Golden Hide than the shops below us, who only include trace amounts just so they can technically claim to be selling Golden Hide-infused fabric. Please, don't hesitate to touch the garment—I'm sure your discerning hands will notice the difference in quality.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Look, her eyes...!
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Though the vendor was facing us, I only saw empty sockets where her eyes should've been.
She's also been... nailed to the ground.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>... Fan your desires... The more you are donned... the higher shall your self ascend...</color>
I understand... These meager patches of—
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Wait, that Voice...!
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: I... heard you. You answered me.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Where are you? Where are you speaking from?
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The vendor thrashed around and reached out toward us, unable to move with the nails that fixed her in place.
This Voice doesn't drag like stretched tape... doesn't stutter... doesn't endlessly speak the same words over and over again...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: No, they are speaking to me... they speak to me...!
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: But... none of us said anything, did we? What's wrong with her?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Where... where did you come from? The Voice to lead us on... the Voice to guide us... ohh, it speaks to me so clearly. This is the Voice I've been searching for my whole life...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: All those days of silence... I see now. They were in anticipation of this beautiful day.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Thank you... Thank you for bringing them to this humble place...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: We don't hear any "voice," unless you're referring to this voice track playing on a loop through your store.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Of course you'd be deaf to it. The Voice speaks only to those who have heard its calling...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The vendor turned slowly, her empty eye sockets scanning through each of us...
... until they came to rest on Meursault.
There they sleep, nestled in your bosom.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: ... In Meursault's bosom?!
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Yes. They have spoken thus—the Voice that once shepherded us has fallen like the setting sun... Mourn we must not, for a new Voice shall rise to lead the flock.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The new Voice slumbers soundly in the Cradle of all threads, its strands undone and taken from all... To them, the world outside is at once a curiosity... and horror...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: When they awaken from their sleep, we will—oh, I can see it... We shall be wreathed in Golden Hide, taken from every fracture of the Grand Magasin...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Alas, we must do our due diligence preparing for their awakening.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: ... And what might that due diligence entail?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: On this floor is an Alterationist's shop. It is said that her scissors are sharp enough to slice through any textile within the Grand Magasin... and her hands dextrous enough to weave any string into fabric.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Then... those keen, precise scissors will one day cut gently into the Cradle,
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: and the fabric woven from her adroit hands will protect the Noirs whose hands shall desecrate the Cradle...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The Alterationist's destiny is to be the root of our bane.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Cutting off the enemy's supply line at its source before the war even starts? That is... tactically sound. Fantastic, even.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Um... But she's not even a part of Le Noir. As far as I know, at least.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: You are correct. She is but a humble, honest Alterationist who merely cuts threads to weave them into fabric.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: But that has changed.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Now that a new Voice has risen on the horizon... all that stands in their way must be... reaped.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: ... And how do you intend to do that "reaping"? You're nailed to the ground.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I have collected many eyeballs during my time here.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Sever the Alterationist, and... all of that will be yours.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Your decision, Executive Manager?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <... Let's not rule it out as an option. We'll have time to decide after we hear out the Noirs on the other side.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <color=#cf0000>Fan your desires... The more you are donned... the higher...</color>
The voice of Meursault's mother, imprinted on the flat surface of an audiotape, repeats and repeats her message from behind the wall of this shop.
But it may as well no longer exist in the vendor's world—she does not turn toward it as she once had, and never will.
That irritating snip-snip has finally stopped... I understand that you have done as I asked?
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Yes, we have. And I'm hoping you'll hold up your end of the bargain.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Of course, of course. Here... take the eyeballs I have gathered.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: ... And... some of them have been holed up inside the whole time...
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: ... Right, I suppose it's only a matter of time before the Grand Magasin falls, now.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: They were never sane to begin with, but now they're growing more and more deranged by the day.
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: Do you think it's true, though? What if they...
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: It really is as the Brand Manager has said.
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: Driven by madness, those abandoned by the Voice have begun to scheme a plan most wicked...
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: ... and they shall join hands with the strangers who have just arrived at the Grand Magasin.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: There wasn't any joining of hands. Let me clarify now that we are not affiliated with either Le Rouge or Le Noir—we'd much rather keep to ourselves than get involved in a war we have no stake in.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: The Voice has prophesied your coming, strangers. That you would come here, after receiving a request to eliminate the Alterationist.
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: Should you bring her harm, we will henceforth declare you enemies of Le Noir. We cannot dispense with the fabric she weaves in times of crisis like the present.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: The Alterationist's importance cannot be overstated. Even the Brand Manager has had to use her fabric to overcome countless trials.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: The Brand Manager has also told us much about your plans. You possess an artifact that is integral to the Rouges' insidious plot, don't you?
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: We'll give you a chance to prove your true allegiance right now, right here.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: Hand over that artifact... and we will greet you as customers, not enemies.
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: <They're... a lot more hostile than they were the first time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... It is likely that the Giant who guides Le Noir has done something behind the scenes.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Oh, yeah. Jeanne remembers the events prior to the loop... then the Noir's Giant must be just as immune to the Liquidation as she is.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Wh-what do we do? I don't know exactly what they're looking for, but... I think they want something from you, Meursault...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Handing over Meursault's artifact will definitely get us into the Noirs' good graces.
Then they'll give us the Authenticity Certificate, and we'll bring that to the One-leg on the—wait, no. That'll just lock us into the same route as before.
<Tell them that we refuse.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We... will not hand anything over to you.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then you are our enemy.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: Strangers, you don't seem to understand the Rouges' true nature, so let me fill you in on just what kind of horror you'd be unleashing.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: The only thing keeping the Grand Magasin from collapse are the patches of the Golden Resin that have grown over its cracks.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: And those red ones... they've been scraping that holy resin from the walls just to wear it as clothes and sate their vain hunger.
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: Their destruction's been long overdue! Do you have any idea how long we've waited for their own greed to come back and bite them?
texts.speaker: Flannel

texts.text: If you still won't hand it over, then... you're no different from them. Which means we'll have to take it from you by force.
texts.speaker: Felt

texts.text: S-so, are we really going to kill Miss Alterationist?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: She wasn't hostile toward us at all, not like these two... Besides, we don't have any reason to do as the Rouge lady asked.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: And we don't have any reason not to do as she asked. Remember: she promised us quite a significant sum of eyeballs in return for slaying the Alterationist.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Yeah, but... do we really need that many eyeballs?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Sinclair doesn't seem as desperate for eyeballs—probably because our Prestige Tier carried over from our last attempt.
He wasn't wrong, either. The only reason we weren't beelining to the fourth floor was that we were still trying to figure out how to get to the fifth floor.

You can never have too much money in your war chest, especially when venturing through unfamiliar territory like this. Unfamiliarity equals unpredictability, and money is one way of mitigating the unknown variables.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: And don't forget, this place isn't real. She won't die just because we killed her in this virtual space where only our minds exist.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: But... But Miss Outis, we don't know what happens to the prisoner's body when their... mind gets killed in here.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: The Executive Manager has already set their mind on what to do.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: The two Sinners can't seem to come to an agreement. But what's really important this time around is...
<I can't make the same choices again and expect things to be different...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... First things first, we need to learn everything we can about the "Liquidation.">
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Meursault, can you call Jeanne and see if she's watching us?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Jeanne. I would like to know more about the conditions to triggering the Liquidation event.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu, ma puce... This is the first time you've decided to call me in here.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>The answer is pretty simple, actually. When the Grand Magasin stops producing Canned Experiences that meet its quality standards, when its output is reduced to useless dregs no one would buy... that's when Liquidation occurs.</color>
... Does the Liquidation process entail rewinding time?
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Nope. Time loops are more trouble than they're worth—gotta make arrangements with T Corp., somehow secure a consistent and massive supply of energy... It's especially impractical now that we can't rely on Lobotomy Corporation for that last part, what with its downfall and all.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Instead, Grand Magasin Sisyphe has chosen to simply... wipe the memories of every customer imprisoned within. It's a relatively simple process, not to mention much, much cheaper. It's a total system reboot, if you will.</color>
<It's just a memory wipe...? So that's why we didn't lose our purchases or the Prestige Tier.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Unfortunately, we can't do a complete reset, which would bring the Grand Magasin back to its very beginning...</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>The seats of all four Giants need to be filled for that process.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>With the present vacancy among the Giants... we've only been able to reset up to a certain point in time, which means that the Canned Experience production rate hasn't been able to match our potential output for a while.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Oh, and don't you two worry—I made sure that only you and your... Manager with that extraordinary hairdo can hear my voice, since you two are trying to keep this between us. Aren't I so thoughtful?</color>
<... I appreciate that.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Manager expresses their appreciation.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Fuhu. I do have a piece of advice for a polite clock like you...</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>I see that you're trying to make different choices from your last attempt, but let me save you the time and effort: it won't matter.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>What do you think the end of the Grand Magasin will look like, ma puce?</color>
... I do not know. I am only following the Manager's judgment.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: But it's your judgment that I'm curious about.
<color=#ebcaa2>Fine. Then let me free that judgment trapped behind your teeth, since you're being annoyingly tight-lipped about it.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>"This Grand Magasin has a predetermined end."</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>"We can keep searching, keep trying, keep struggling—but it won't change how it ends. Which makes everything we're doing... everything we're racking our brains to solve... simply pointless."</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Hey, why don't you... go on a shopping spree instead? Make yourself stand out to the world. Come on, you're in a department store for heaven's sake!</color>
<... Thank her for the advice. But we'll continue to explore all of our options.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Manager's judgment remains the same, Jeanne.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>I've seen so many customers come into this place, determined and ready to fight against its currents... only for them to rapidly settle into the Grand Magasin's system like compliant little lambs.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Well, while you keep yourselves busy with that silly business, I'll sit nicely in this corner and be a quiet witness to your adventures. I've been one for a long, long time anyway.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>... I should go brew myself a steaming hot cup of coffee. I'll take my time until it cools down nicely, and by the time I take the final sip...</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>You know what I'm talking about, don't you, ma puce?</color>
Is everything alright, Executive Manager? You've been muttering to yourself for a while.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Ah. I've just been lost in thought, that's all.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Alright, let's, uh... let's do as that Rouge asked. Next stop's the Alteration Shop.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Heh. Excellent choice, Executive Manager.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I watch Outis and Sinclair arguing about random trivialities as they prepare to head to the Alteration Shop.
Neither of them knows...
... that we'd already reached the "end" once and had woken up on the first floor like nothing had happened.
<Do you think we'll be able to... reach a different outcome this time?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes, we will be able to reach a different outcome. However, as Jeanne has said...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... it will be irrelevant to preventing the Liquidation process.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <... I'll be honest, I'm feeling a bit lost. I don't have any clues... let alone any hope of finding one.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I see that you haven't let that slow your pace, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Meursault regards me as if he's scrutinizing me.
Was that supposed to be a question? Or just his way of expressing doubt?
<Well, this isn't the first time we've landed ourselves in a hopeless situation.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <I'm sure it won't be our last, either.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... Or maybe I'm just choosing not to believe Jeanne. She said the end won't change no matter what we do, but... we haven't tried it yet, have we?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yeah. More often than not, our journey so far has been full of unreasonable absurdities like these.
I decided that, therefore, it was unreasonable of me to expect that the solution would be delivered to us on a silver platter.
Then... What can we do?
Just keep on keeping on, I guess.
<Let's try doing things differently this time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <I know we might just end up proving Jeanne right, and maybe nothing will change from our last attempt. But we can cross that bridge when we get to it.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... A-am I being too irresponsible?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... If that is how you have judged this situation, Manager, then I will do as ordered.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Welcome back, strangers with drooping shoulder seams.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: ... But you're not here to have something mended, are you?
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: It's, uh—
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: The hand that comes to caress the string and the hand that comes to sever it make different sounds on contact with my doorknob.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: This time, your visit is to... see me severed.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: ... You're quick to notice... Yes, it is... We won't deny it.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... So, the strangers have chosen to stand with the Rouges. It seems they have found themselves more than one salvation.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Not to worry, strangers. There is little difference between what you are doing and alteration work. When you have chosen the part of the fabric to mend the attire with, the remaining half joins the scrap pile.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: But let's be fair. If you would like to cut me away... you'd better have come prepared to be snipped away yourselves.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: We are prepared.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I can see the desire to go snip-snip! in your eyes.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: I like that look.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Unlike our last attempt... I may be able to adjourn the meeting.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Yeah? Then... it's all yours.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Still full of meeting.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Disturb the meeting, and you'll become two.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: ... You're pretty good.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: The path is now... locked. Whatever the Rouges choose to weave into existence now, it cannot be undone. You have irrevocably made yourselves enemies of the Noirs.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Cutting... is not the sole purpose of scissors... Sometimes... scissors are the only means... to untangle a knotted mess of strings...
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Take my scissors with you... strangers... with drooping shoulder seams...
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: You have beheld the pulse... I'm sure... you'll make... good use of it...
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: The Alterationist stirs no longer.
<Let's take her pair of scissors and return to the Rouge vendor.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: We ripped the pair of scissors—which might even have been her skeleton, now that I'm getting a better look—off the Alterationist's torso.
Once we removed the pair of scissors, the rest of the Alterationist's body crumbled like an article of clothing removed from its hanging rack.
Can't go this way.
... Still full of meeting.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Disturb the meeting, and you'll become two.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: ... Still full of meeting.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Disturb the meeting, and you'll become two.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Do you need anything altered?
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: I can patch, and I can mend. Which would you like?
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: We emerged into a round room whose walls were lined with multicolored spools of thread and swaths of cut fabric. At the center stood a figure, her arms moving up and down as she stitched something together in a carefully regulated rhythm.
Um... Hello?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Shoulder seams hanging a touch too low... hems of the arm a span too short. Much work to be done, this one. So, what would you like to have altered?
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: We would like to procure a pair of scissors.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... What? Scissors?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: ... My scissors are not tools to be hung and sold from the product racks. I do not part with my blades for just anyone, you see.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: They're reserved for customers whose eyes twinkle with the desire to go snip-snip. Like the Noirs, my longtime customers—they always visit me to have me weave fabric for them.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: Are you... well-acquainted with the Noirs?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: I've been regularly supplying them with fabric for a while now, so one could say that we are partners.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: The Noirs have been quite busy as of late—spreading and fishing tales, suspicious that the red ones are up to no good.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: I simply do not see that same passionate desire in you. I do have other items available for purchase, however.
texts.speaker: Annette the Alterationist

texts.text: <Looks like getting straight to the point won't work on her... This isn't what happened last time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Perhaps... we could procure the pair of scissors at our next opportunity, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Don't think we have any other choice.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: So... why did we need a pair of scissors, again?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Scissors, when honed to perfection, make excellent weapons. Haven't you come to understand by now that every action the Executive Manager takes is backed up by perfectly reasonable explanations?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Executive Manager, it appears that their only response will be to repeat "we're in a meeting" ad nauseam.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... Yeah, no need to talk to them.
The Voice... has now seeeeettt...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: Yet do not griiieeeeve...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: <Hmm... I don't know what deal we can offer this one.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Attempts to communicate with this being may be futile.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Doooonnnn... The more you are Doooonnneed...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: <Don't think we have any business with them...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Floor Manager speaks no more.
Doooooo nooooot...! Griiiiieeeeve...!!!
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: A neonate vooooooooice shaaaaallllll...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: Ah... Looks like it's you and me for this floor, Outis.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Feels a bit strange, doesn't it? Having to go around with a different group on every floor.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Still, I'm glad to be partnered up with you for this floor. It's been easier for us to work together lately, so...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: What? No, I'm not "easy" with anyone, least of all you Sinners. Ridiculous.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Riiight...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Hey. I need to ask you something.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Outis fixed a quizzical look toward Meursault, who looked completely unfazed by everything that should be, for all intents and purposes, as unfamiliar as the world is to a newborn.
No, I have not been in here before. I was told about this place by someone in a managerial position within the Grand Magasin Sisyphe.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Have you b— What?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Meursault's succinct reply came almost simultaneously as Outis had begun her query, but it answered everything she was about to ask.
Whiplashed by the speed with which Meursault answered, she stumbled over her words for a moment before clearing her throat and continuing with her next question.
What was the nature of your relationship with that individual?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... The romantic kind. Once.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>The kind that gets... pretty steamy.</color>
Who said that?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Pfft... Still got that excellent memory, huh?</color>
The voice came through with clarity, but it carried a note of sadness.
And... I'd come to be intimately acquainted with the name of the speaker.
<color=#ebcaa2>Ah, here we go again. Time to introduce myself.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>My name is... Jeanne. That's the name of the Voice I've so graciously chosen to share with you this time as well.</color>
Huh, looks like they're blocking the way through.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <... Talking to those things'll probably achieve nothing, but...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Excuse me, would you let us into the store behind you?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Meeting! So much meeting!
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: So no entry. No room for anything else.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: What's the taste of meeting?
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Salty, so salty. Salty like tears. Too salty for anyone to swallow.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Meeting won't end. Swallow meeting to end debate. But can't swallow.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: ... So, what's this meeting about?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Agenda 1: Who is the outer fabric, and who is the lining?
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Agenda 2: Who is the right hand, and who is the left hand?
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Mmm, mmm. Good agendas. Let's write them both in the minutes.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Approaching them might be dangerous... Should we come back here later?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <Don't think we have any other choice.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Huh? Weren't they further down the other side of the corridor earlier?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <Yeah. When'd they get here?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Crawled here. Creepy-creep.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Meeting's over.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Agenda: Warm aroma. Aroma of life. Whose is it?
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: So we creepy-creep. Encroaching. Creepy-creep. Narrowing the gap.
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: <Hey, Meursault... I think they might be...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... after that piece of flesh you're carrying.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That appears to be the likely explanation.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Tsk... We're going to have to circumnavigate that monster to reach the other side, Executive Manager.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <There's a way south of the Rouge shop. Maybe we can take that route to the other side.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Huh? That didn't take very long.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: As expedient as always, Executive Manager—hm?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... What is that thing behind you?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <The... true form of the new "Voice" the Rouges have been talking about. I think.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <One of the Rouges asked us to look after them, so... we decided to let the kid tag along for a while.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I see... So why are they standing so far away from us?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: The child appears to be apprehensive of our presence.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Hmm... Doesn't appear to pose us any threats at the moment...
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... but you don't want to have entities of dubitable intent following from behind, Executive Manager—I implore you to remain vigilant. Unlike your ever-so-faithful and trustworthy Outis, there is always a threat of backstabbing from such unknown factors.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Y-yeah...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Anyway, since we're here to show the kid to the Rouge vendor, let's head to her shop.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ah... Ahh... You have brought them to me... I am truly blessed...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Oh, dearest Voice, revered be your presence... I have prepared a humble gift in anticipation of your promised advent...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Please... Please take this.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The vendor produced a red handkerchief—clearly of her make—and carefully placed it on the child's hands.
She withdrew with visible reverence, and seeing the child hold her creation, began to tremble like she was a bomb about to go off.
Aaaaah... They accepted it! They accepted my creation...!
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Nothing could ever make me happier than this... Oh, my God... I have no more needs... Take me, I am yours...!
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: What's happ— ...! Take cover, Executive Manager!
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Aaaahhhh!? S-she exploded!
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Are you unhurt? Has any of that filth—
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <I'm— I'm fine.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Nnh... Uu...
<... Didn't see that coming.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... So you haven't experienced this before.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: When I looked up, the child had already scurried off to a distance it seemed to have determined safe from us... Something about that made my heart ache a little.
<I wonder if the Rouge's spinal cord will be important again?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That cannot be said for certain. However, it is recommended that we bring with us any object that may potentially be useful.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <... Yeah, let's take that with us and head right upstairs.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Understood.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The corpse of a Noir. Even the fabric they took such pride in couldn't save them from this fate.

[Differential of Falling Series 1: "Cynthia"
This installation depicts the fall of Cynthia, the first Mannequin to fall in the Grand Magasin. The only large-scale installation in the series, it sets itself apart from the rest of the series by being the only piece to depict the precise moment her fall began in painstaking detail.]
Dooooo noooot griiiieeeeve... Dooooo noooot griiiieeeeve...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: A voice once set... like the fallen sun... will never return...
texts.speaker: 3F Floor Manager

texts.text: When too much has become tangled together, the only choice is to sever them.
As Meursault scooped the veritable hillock of eyeballs into our sack, the vendor, who had been quietly nodding away into the ether, turned toward us.
Ah... of course. Anything you say.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: The Voice summons you... They are summoning the strangers there to the Luxury Hall. The promised hour of awakening is nigh...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: We can't even hear that "Voice" of yours. Did they say anything about what they want with us?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Yeah, that's kinda weird. Shouldn't they be summoning the rest of the Rouges, not us?
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: We are bound by the rules of the Grand Magasin. Only on special occasions are we permitted to freely traverse between its floors. Only true strangers, whose presence the Fount welcomes, are free to rise and descend.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: You carry the shard of our cherished one within you. Once you assemble the final piece, they will awaken.
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Ahh... This is what I sacrificed my eyes for... and let myself be nailed to the ground... All in service of this day...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Blessed with an eternity of nailed existence to convey the Voice's will to the promised strangers... Ah, what a joyous day... What a joyous day...
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: Suppose we are to do as this "Voice" asks. Where would we find this "Luxury Hall"?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <I know where it is. We stopped by the entrance on the second floor earlier.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Then the true form of the Voice must be waiting for us there.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <There was a... cocoon the Rouges were caring for.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We ripped it open with a nail and killed the thing that crawled out of it.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Yeah. Then... the Noirs took over the Grand Magasin... triggering the Liquidation process. Which means...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The end of the Grand Magasin we witnessed was ultimate "stagnation."
All lives within the department store were consolidated into a single purpose: to become pillars to perpetuate its existence...
Eternity passed within the Grand Magasin, devoid of any change—even shopping.
And as eternity came and went, everything became integrated, seamlessly assimilated with the walls of the Grand Magasin.
In the end, not even the smallest stir survived. All was melded into everything and everyone... including us.
If only I hadn't ripped open and torn that thing out of the cocoon...
<Let's descend, Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: You intend to ally with the Rouges as a means of climbing the Grand Magasin.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Yeah. It's kinda hard to explain why, but... I have a feeling that that's what I must do this time.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That inexplicable sort of intuition is an indispensable quality in a commander. Those without it... did not survive the War for long, no matter how excellent their other abilities were.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Looks like this is where we get off. Good work, everyone.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: ... In my experience, recognizing the hand of fate doesn't necessarily mean that one can break free from its grip, Executive Manager.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Outis...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ah. Apologies, I overstepped. I'd witnessed and heard far too many tales of a similar nature that... the present circumstance must've put me in a contemplative mood.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Tsk. I would much rather serve you by your side at all times, Executive Manager... It is regrettable that I won't be able to.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: A [Prêt-à-porter] display rack.
Outis once told me that it's a communication switchboard.
It says [Origami CollectioN° 92, 2 of 5. Someone's fall sublimated into superpositioned time.]
The fuck're you lookin' at! Get lost, fuckwit!
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: <... I see. This couch came from the Furniture Hall.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <At least this room is well-lit.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Meeting still underway!
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: The meeting must go on, they said!
texts.speaker: Two-piece

texts.text: Ooh... Voice...! Help me... Must I suffer death now, when you have finally come to grace me?!
texts.speaker: L'Inamovible

texts.text: <Damn, thought we dodged that.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That enemy presents difficulties on multiple fronts... Its speed is one thing, but it has the uncanny ability to swerve at the last minute to follow Meursault's attempt to evade.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I recommend using the environmental obstacles or employing more unpredictable evasive maneuvers.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <... Of course. Let's try this again.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Can't get a good grasp on when it'll explode...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We'll have to move away as soon as it begins to tremble.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: Try to stay more alert next time.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: It will be done.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: It is quite fast for its size.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: How should Meursault dodge its charge...? Maybe there's a way to perfectly time a block, but I don't think that'll be easy.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: While it may seem as though there is no room to properly evade its charge, there were small indents at both ends of the room—perhaps you could hide there?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <Oh, right. I don't think it can reach that far.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: As for the rest of the battle strategy... A more deliberate approach will be effective, Executive Manager. Take your time fending off the onslaught of Mobiles and slowly wear down the primary foe.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... Tsk. I know it's your "turn," but this must still be incredibly taxing.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Once we return, I'll be sure to assign the cleaning duties to the ones lounging around in the restroom.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: So... hold on just a little longer.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I will.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... That thing ripped him in half the moment they came into contact.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: We may have to wait until their "meeting" is adjourned, Executive Manager.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Honestly, those agendas didn't really seem all that important...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <Either way, let's steer clear of that thing until we find a way around it.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Ah, here it is. "Series 2.">
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: A close observation the floor beneath the installation has revealed nothing, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Nngh... I assume all these "Mannequins" are just people, too.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text:
[Differential of Falling Series 3: "Stockmann"
This installation was inspired by a Mannequin's fall through the Grand Magasin. The imagery evokes the falling continuity of time.
Sculpted in a smaller size relative to the Series 1 installation.]
<This is the last one in the series, I think...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ah...! There's something written on the leather here.
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: [... Artworks made from human corpus for cheap shock value are now long outmoded in the current zeitgeist.]
[But... this department store doesn't seem to have gotten the news.]
[I'm running out of material. Running out of inspiration. No one here really appreciates my art—they're all obsessed with clothes and nothing more. Then...]
[... But these sell well. Le Rouge seems to somewhat value these... sorry excuse for artwork that the world outside regards as nothing more than mass-produced garbage...]
[If they're worth something to them, I can sell these, make money—eyeballs. Then I'll buy better clothes, then I'll—]
<There are more installations like this one, but those didn't have any titles attached to them.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Perhaps they were too ashamed to attach their name to these artworks, but the more likely explanation is simply that...
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: ... they've forgotten what artwork they were trying to create, or the fact that it was artwork at all.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: <... They've become a customer.>
texts.speaker: Dante
